status_summary: EPA ended its environmental justice and DEI units on 2025-03-12, and its fiscal year 2026 reorganization addendum (September 2025) states that the Office of Environmental Justice and External Civil Rights and the ten regional environmental justice divisions were eliminated, with accessibility and external civil rights work moved to an Office of Civil Rights in the Administrator's office. The addendum also created an Office of Applied Science and Environmental Solutions, moved Office of Research and Development scientists into program offices, merged the Chief Financial Officer's office with most of the Office of Mission Support into an Office of Finance and Administration, and eliminated ten organizational units in the Office of Enforcement and Compliance Assurance. The Mandate called for eliminating that enforcement office and restructuring the Office of International and Tribal Affairs, but EPA's organization chart page (updated 2026-09-09) still lists both offices. EPA reported in July 2025 a workforce falling from 16,155 to 12,448; its budget page lists a fiscal year 2026 enacted workforce of 12,312, and the fiscal year 2027 request is $4.203 billion (52 percent below fiscal year 2026 enacted) with 12,500 FTE and up to $20 million to optimize office and laboratory space. The Budget in Brief proposes releasing office space in high-cost areas of regional offices, and E&E News reported space consolidation in Regions 5 and 9, but no regional office relocation plan, General Counsel consolidation of enforcement attorneys or tribal office restructuring was found.

timeline.event: EPA announced it was ending its environmental justice and DEI offices, placing employees in both on administrative leave and citing the executive order on DEI programs.

EPA announced a next phase of reorganization: a new Office of Applied Science and Environmental Solutions in the Office of the Administrator, a new Office of State Air Partnerships and a new Office of Clean Air Programs in the Office of Air and Radiation; EPA stated that employment would return to levels near the Reagan administration and that this phase would save more than 300 million dollars a year by fiscal year 2026.

EPA announced a reduction in force affecting the Office of Research and Development, citing 748.8 million dollars in savings and a workforce falling from 16,155 in January 2025 to about 12,448; the release states the earlier environmental justice and DEI action involved a reduction in force of 280 employees and the transfer of 195 employees.

An EPA fiscal year 2026 budget addendum on consolidation and reorganization (month-level date from the file path, first of month used) describes eliminating the Office of Environmental Justice and External Civil Rights and the ten regional environmental justice divisions, creating the Office of Applied Science and Environmental Solutions, dissolving the Office of Research and Development's structure by moving scientists into program offices, merging the Chief Financial Officer's office with most of the Office of Mission Support into an Office of Finance and Administration, and eliminating ten units in the Office of Enforcement and Compliance Assurance, which is retained. It does not mention the international and tribal office or the General Counsel.

EPA's Region 9 office was scheduled to begin consolidating staff into less office space (month-only date), with space to be returned to the General Services Administration by 2026-08-05, and Region 5 was reported to be giving up two floors in Chicago; EPA described the changes as routine space management, not a relocation of regional offices.

EPA's fiscal year 2027 Budget in Brief (filed under April 2026, exact day not confirmed, first of month used) proposes $4.203 billion and 12,500 FTE, a 52 percent decrease from fiscal year 2026 enacted, continues realignments, and proposes up to $20 million to optimize office and laboratory space, including laboratory consolidation and releasing space in high-cost areas of regional offices.

EPA's organization chart page (last updated on this date) lists ten headquarters offices, including the Office of Enforcement and Compliance Assurance, the Office of Finance and Administration and the Office of International and Tribal Affairs, and does not list a stand-alone Office of Research and Development or American Indian Environmental Office.

title: Reorganize EPA: close environmental justice offices, restructure science, cut staff
uncertainties: The 16,155 baseline and 12,448 target come from EPA's July 2025 release (headcount), while the 14,130 and 12,312 budget-page figures are FTE ceilings, so they are not directly comparable. EPA's 2025-05-02 release states 175 employees were transferred from the environmental justice and DEI offices while its 2025-07-18 release states 195; the difference was not resolved. The fiscal year 2026 addendum carries no calendar date on its face and the 2025-09-01 date is taken from the file path; the Budget in Brief is dated 2026-04-01 from its file path. The addendum describes planned and completed changes without separate effective dates. The organization chart page lists only top-level offices, so the absence of the American Indian Environmental Office there is not proof it was abolished. A PEER complaint to the Office of Special Counsel on behalf of environmental justice staff, reported by a Harvard tracker with inconsistent dates, is not in the timeline because it is not a government action. The Region 5 and 9 space consolidation rests on a 2025-12-02 E&E News report of an internal EPA email and a union statement; the January 2026 start is the scheduled date, and whether it began on time was not confirmed. The Budget in Brief was read on the space optimization and totals but not in full. No Federal Register notice of the reorganization was searched. Litigation outcomes are unknown. Not verified: Office of Public Engagement, Children's Health Protection and Small and Disadvantaged Business Utilization changes, and any EPA statement on General Counsel consolidation.
